newsitem.title: USA: Graco has positive outlook for 1997.
newsitem.headline: Graco has positive outlook for 1997.

text.p: Graco Inc, after posting solid second-half results Monday, said it remains cautious but is entering 1997 with a strong outlook.

"While 1996 started out slowly, due to factors including harsh winter conditions in North America, the second half of the year was strong," George Aristides, president and chief executive, said in a statement.
"Although we remain cautious about economic conditions in our markets, the overall outlook for 1997 is positive," he said.

Earlier, Graco which provides technology for the management of fluids in both industrial and commercial applications, reported fourth quarter earnings of $0.60 a share versus $0.41 last year. Earnings for the year were $2.07 a share compared with $1.59 in 1995.

At the end of the quarter, backlog was $19 million, compared with $20 million at the end of 1995 and $33 million at the end of the third quarter of 1996. Graco said the drop in backlog is primarily due to the shipment of several large engineered systems.

During the fourth quarter, the company said its gross profit margin declined to 48 percent, due primarily to the increased proportion of large engineered systems shipments, the company said. Operating margin expanded by 2.8 percentage points as the result of higher sales.
Stock repurchases under Graco's announced share buyback program totaled about 400,000 shares in 1996, the company said.
